title: Concentrating Viruses via PEG precipitation
author: Jozef Nissimov
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.d9j94m
materials: Distribute into four sterile 250 mL centrifuge bottles.

steps.title: Add NaCl and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 58.4 g NaCl to 1 L of lysate filtered through a 0.45 µm membrane (or 0.2 µm for smaller viruses), dissolve gently, and let stand on ice or at 4 °C for at least 2 h.

steps.title: Centrifuge to collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the bottles at 5000 rpm, 4 °C for 2 h; retain the supernatant.

steps.title: Combine supernatants
steps.instruction: Combine the supernatants from the four bottles into an autoclaved sterile 1 L glass bottle.

steps.title: Add PEG and incubate
steps.instruction: Add PEG 6000 (Sigma) to achieve a final concentration of 10 % w/v (i.e., 100 g PEG per 1 L), dissolve gently, and let stand on ice or at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and pellet wash
steps.instruction: Divide the mixture into four sterile 250 mL centrifuge bottles, centrifuge at 6000 rpm, 4 °C for 50 min, discard the supernatant, and invert the tubes on paper towels for a few minutes.

substeps.instruction: Divide into four sterile 250 mL centrifuge bottles.
Invert tubes on paper towels for a few minutes.

steps.title: Resuspend pellets and store
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 3 mL of a suitable buffer (phage buffer, phosphate buffer, or Tris buffer), combine the four resuspensions to a total of 12 mL in a Falcon tube, and store at 4 °C until further processing (e.g., CsCl gradient or CTAB DNA extraction).
